Please refresh **http://maker:4001**. Let's look at what happens in the *awkward* moments:

**Edge 1 — empty read-later list.** With no links yet opted into read-later, click the **To read** tab. Instead of a blank area, you get a gentle explanation of how to add things to read-later. Does that feel helpful?

**Edge 2 — a page whose title can't be fetched.** Save a link using this address: `https://notitle.example.com/page`. After the "Fetching…" moment, the app can't get a title, so it **falls back to showing the address** and displays an amber note telling you it couldn't fetch the title and you can Rename it. Does handling a failed title this way (save it anyway, show the address, let you rename) match what you'd want — rather than blocking the save?

**Edge 3 — something that isn't a real link.** In the save box, type plain nonsense like `not a link` and press Save. It's refused with an inline message rather than saving a broken entry. Is refusing clearly-invalid input the behaviour you'd expect?

And one situation I can't fully show on screen, so let me just ask about the intended behaviour:

**Edge 4 — saving the same link twice.** If you save a link you've already saved before, what would you prefer — that the app quietly lets you have two copies, or that it **notices the duplicate and warns you** (so your list doesn't fill with repeats)?
